solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: As table shows, London team lost last two, I note

indicators.note: the team's name is docked its final pair of letters, as if it had lost its last two games

parts.note: Arsenal is a north London football club
C is a musical note

explanation.surface: A football fan reads the league table: a London club has dropped its last two games.
explanation.walkthrough: 'As table shows' is not a league table but the periodic table, where As is the symbol of the element; 'lost last two' takes AL off ARSENAL to leave ARSEN.
explanation.definitionFit: In the periodic table of chemical elements, As is the symbol given to arsenic.

clue.text: Be resigned to move to restrict Church parking

indicators.note: restricting something hems it in, so this word encloses the others

parts.note: to act is to take a step or move
CE is the Church of England
P is the map symbol for parking

explanation.surface: Someone must put up with a move to limit parking at the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To accept a situation is to tolerate it without protest, resigning yourself to it.

clue.text: Referring to environment, small/medium enterprise penning fine release

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, as in a pen, so this word encloses another

parts.note: SME is the standard abbreviation for a small or medium-sized enterprise
OK means fine, all right
to free is to release

explanation.surface: An environmental report on a small business handling a fine and a release.
explanation.definitionFit: A smoke-free environment is one where tobacco smoking is banned.

clue.text: Nothing odd in unease — avoid showing birthmarks

indicators.note: take nothing from the odd positions, so only the even letters of the following words are kept

explanation.surface: Someone advises not letting worry about blemishes show.
explanation.walkthrough: The even letters of UNEASE give NAE and those of AVOID give VI; 'showing' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A naevus is a mole or coloured mark on the skin present from birth; naevi is the plural.

clue.text: From Denver maybe, can do oral that's rearranged

indicators.note: rearranged signals the letters are put into a different order

explanation.surface: A speaker from Denver can manage a rearranged oral exam.
explanation.definitionFit: Denver is the capital of the US state of Colorado, so a resident is a Coloradan.

clue.text: Church garment cold when blow encountered

parts.note: C is the abbreviation for cold, as on a tap
as can mean when, as in 'as I left'
a sock is a hard punch or blow

explanation.surface: A clergyman's robe proves chilly when he meets a strong gust of wind.
explanation.definitionFit: A cassock is the long robe worn by clergy and choristers, a vestment of the church.

clue.text: Took an interest as Jack, say, consumed energy

indicators.note: consumed means swallowed, so this word takes the other inside it

parts.note: a jack is an example of a playing card
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone called Jack showed concern while using up his energy.
explanation.definitionFit: Cared is the past tense of care, meaning felt concern or attention.

clue.text: Alexander with German boat crew maybe, in vehicle

parts.note: Sandy is a pet form of Alexander
acht is German for eight, and an eight is a rowing crew

explanation.surface: Alexander and a German rowing crew travel in a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sand yacht is a wheeled craft with a sail, driven by wind across beaches.

clue.text: External computer equipment with top removed

indicators.note: in a down clue the top is the first letter, which is dropped

parts.note: a router is a device linking computers to a network

explanation.surface: Outside computer hardware is supplied with its cover off.
explanation.definitionFit: Outer means on the outside, the opposite of inner.

clue.text: Memento of castle, drink to follow

indicators.note: to follow means this word comes after the previous one

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle
sake is Japanese rice wine

explanation.surface: A souvenir from a castle, with a drink afterwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A keepsake is a small item kept in memory of a person or place.

clue.text: Near end

explanation.walkthrough: Two meanings, pronounced differently: the adjective with a soft S and the noun with a hard Z sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is an adjective for nearness and also a noun for the finish of something.

clue.text: Unusually let go — rent viewing aid

indicators.note: unusually signals the letters are put in an unexpected, rearranged order

explanation.surface: A landlord oddly lets a tenant off the rent.
explanation.definitionFit: A lorgnette is a pair of spectacles held up on a handle, an old-fashioned aid to seeing.

clue.text: Country leader's meeting with media boss shown for first time

indicators.note: meeting with places the second piece directly beside the first

parts.note: a premier is the head of a country's government
ED is short for editor, the boss of a newspaper

explanation.surface: A prime minister's encounter with a newspaper editor is publicised for the first time.
explanation.definitionFit: A film or play that premiered was given its first public performance.

clue.text: Battles here — quite so, about limits on power

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so one piece goes round the other

parts.note: yes is an agreeing reply, like 'quite so'

indicators.note: limits are the edges, so the first and last letters of the word

explanation.surface: Someone agrees, mentioning the restrictions on power.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Battles here' reads like a statement about fighting, but it defines a place: the Belgian town fought over repeatedly in the First World War.
explanation.definitionFit: Ypres in Belgium was the site of several major First World War battles.

clue.text: Doctor raced and took lunch without stopping

indicators.note: to doctor is to tamper with, so the letters are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: A medic hurried off and had a meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' reads as a person but is the anagram signal; 'and' just joins, and the letters of RACED, TOOK and LUNCH are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Working round the clock means continuously, all day and all night with no break.

clue.text: Indicate importance of policy following foreign articles

indicators.note: following means this word comes after the earlier one

parts.note: un is a French article and der a German one
a line is a policy, as in the party line

explanation.surface: A policy is stressed after some articles from abroad.
explanation.definitionFit: To underline a point is to emphasise it, literally by drawing a line beneath text.

clue.text: Like some footwear he passed on before November — cheered about that

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the cheering word goes round what comes before

parts.note: to hail is to greet with cheers

indicators.note: before puts this piece ahead of the next

parts.note: ob. is short for Latin obiit, he died, seen on memorials
N is November in the radio alphabet

explanation.surface: A man died before November and was cheered about it.
explanation.walkthrough: The abbreviation ob. (obiit, Latin for 'he died') appears on gravestones and in reference books, so 'he passed on' gives it as a single piece.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobnailed boots have short heavy-headed nails driven into the soles for grip and wear.

clue.text: Eager to be transformative with poor musical drama one sees often

indicators.note: being transformative means changing things, so the letters are changed into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone keen for poor musical theatre to change lives.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters of EAGER and POOR are rearranged; 'with' just joins the two.
explanation.definitionFit: An operagoer is a person who attends performances of opera regularly.

clue.text: Clouds over revised courses initially brought in

indicators.note: in signals one piece placed inside the other
revised means altered, so the letters are put in a new order
initially means the first letter is taken

explanation.surface: Clouds pass over altered courses at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: COURSES rearranged gives OSCURES, and the first letter of 'brought' goes in; 'over' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: To obscure something is to conceal it or make it hard to see, as clouds hide the sun.

clue.text: Not fancy money with laughing-stock — ditherer's statement

parts.note: bread is slang for money
and means together with
the butt of a joke is the person laughed at
er is the sound a hesitating speaker makes

explanation.surface: Someone hesitates over cash and a figure of fun.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread-and-butter describes something basic and everyday, plain rather than elaborate.

clue.text: Vegetable — moving fast, it vanishes

indicators.note: vanishes means the named letters disappear from the word

parts.note: celerity is swiftness of movement

explanation.surface: A vegetable disappears because it is moving so quickly.
explanation.definitionFit: Celery is a vegetable with long crisp stalks, eaten raw or cooked.

clue.text: Easily seen in vehicle, a runabout

indicators.note: in signals that the answer sits inside the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: Something is visible in a small car used for getting about.
explanation.definitionFit: Clear can mean plainly visible or obvious to the eye.

clue.text: Praise once charge cut

parts.note: ex means former, once

indicators.note: cut means the word is trimmed of its last letter

parts.note: a toll is a charge for using a road or bridge

explanation.surface: Someone welcomes a fee that was once reduced.
explanation.definitionFit: To extol is to praise someone or something enthusiastically.

clue.text: Marked by complexity — add more details

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the adjective, intricate and detailed
second meaning: the verb, to expand on something

explanation.walkthrough: The adjective and verb are spelt alike but stressed differently.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means intricate; the verb means to expand on a point with further information.

clue.text: Diplomat in hidden voyage…

indicators.note: in signals that the answer is contained in the run of words that follows

explanation.surface: An official is concealed on a secret journey.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hidden' looks like the signal but is part of the text: the answer straddles 'hidden voyage', and 'in' is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: An envoy is a messenger or representative sent on a diplomatic mission.

clue.text: …also very involved in sports grounds maybe

indicators.note: involved means tangled, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: Continuing the previous clue: the envoy is also much caught up in sports venues.
explanation.definitionFit: Many sports grounds are oval-shaped, like the Oval cricket ground in London, so ovals is a shape example.

clue.text: Getting back, seeing English quintet in second hearing

indicators.note: in signals the pieces placed inside the other word

parts.note: a retrial is a case heard in court a second time
V is the Roman numeral five, a group of five

explanation.surface: An English group of five musicians appears in court again.
explanation.definitionFit: Retrieval is the act of recovering or fetching something back.

clue.text: Home of President hosting returning party

indicators.note: a host holds guests, so this word takes another inside it

parts.note: Abe is Abraham Lincoln, US President

indicators.note: returning means the word for party is read backwards

parts.note: a do is a party

explanation.surface: A president's residence hosts a party on his return.
explanation.definitionFit: An abode is a dwelling, the place where someone lives.

clue.text: Singular, verily, recollected as having clear, ringing sound

parts.note: S is the grammatical abbreviation for singular

indicators.note: re-collected, gathered again in a new arrangement, so the letters are shuffled

explanation.surface: An archaic speaker truly remembers a pure, bell-like tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'recollected' looks like remembering but reads as re-collected: the letters of VERILY gathered again in a new order.
explanation.definitionFit: A silvery voice or bell has a soft, clear and melodious tone.

clue.text: Ruin of French second city, old

parts.note: de is French for of
Troy is the ancient city of Greek legend

explanation.surface: The ruins of an old French city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ruin' looks like a noun but is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To ruin something is to wreck or demolish it completely.
